title: India's first rocket parts arrived at the launch site by bicycle and bullock cart.

sources.text: ISRO - Diamond Jubilee of the First Sounding Rocket Launch
The Better India - The story of India's first rocket launch from Thumba

caption:
India's first rocket parts arrived at the launch site by bicycle and bullock cart.

The US-supplied Nike-Apache rocket carried a French payload and a local church, St. Mary Magdalene, was converted into an early assembly facility and control room. Vikram Sarabhai and a young Abdul Kalam were both central to the launch.

The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station built around that first launch grew into the infrastructure base for India's entire space program, from early sounding rockets to Chandrayaan and Gaganyaan decades later.

India's space program didn't begin with a launch pad. It began with a fishing village, a church and two scientists willing to improvise their way to orbit.
